page.layout: One page of text in a single column. At the top, a continuation of a verse passage (italic) from the previous page, then a horizontal rule. Below it, a centred heading and a poem with a large initial O. Below the poem, a decorative woodcut ornament with no text. A catchword at the right margin, below the ornament. The running head is at the top, and the page number is at the top left.

l.i: Quíque faber docti fugit organa nosse Lycæi
Artis utérque suæ tum sedulus organa tractans
Organa docta faber nescit tractare Tubingus
Quæ vera monstrant cum ratione loqui.
Ergo cum Sterope, Brontéque fabrilia tractans
Malleus atque incus gemini cum forcipe folles,
Indocto sunt hæc organa digna fabro.

page.notes: The ornament below the poem is a circular floral woodcut with no text. The printed "IN" at the lower right is a catchword. The large initial O of the poem is joined to "rgana" as "Organa". The first verse stanza is a continuation from the previous page. Long s is transcribed as s throughout, so "dedifcet" is read as "dediscet" and "monftrant" as "monstrant". The accents on "docti", "forcipibusque" and "Brontéque" were read with some uncertainty.
